payload.title: Bones, muscles and organs of the body

explanations.Mandible: The jawbone, the movable bone of the lower jaw in the head.
explanations.Sternum: The breastbone, a flat bone in the centre of the chest.
explanations.Lumbar vertebra: One of the five bones of the lower spine, lying between the rib cage and the pelvis.
explanations.Masseter: The chewing muscle of the jaw, which raises the lower jaw.
explanations.Diaphragm: The sheet of muscle at the base of the chest that draws air into the lungs.
explanations.Rectus abdominis: The long paired muscle down the front of the abdomen.
explanations.Brain: The central organ of the nervous system, protected by the skull.
explanations.Heart: The organ that pumps blood, sitting between the lungs in the middle of the chest.
explanations.Liver: The large metabolic organ in the upper right of the abdomen.

sources.excerpt: In jawed vertebrates, the mandible (from the Latin mandibula, 'for chewing'), lower jaw, or jawbone is a bone that makes up the lower – and typically more mobile – component of the mouth (the upper jaw being known as the maxilla).
The sternum (pl.: sternums or sterna) or breastbone is a long flat bone located in the central part of the chest.
In human anatomy, the five lumbar vertebrae are between the rib cage and the pelvis.
In anatomy, the masseter is one of the muscles of mastication.
The action of the muscle during bilateral contraction of the entire muscle is to elevate the mandible, raising the lower jaw.

The diaphragm is the most important muscle of respiration, and separates the thoracic cavity, containing the heart and lungs, from the abdominal cavity: as the diaphragm contracts, the volume of the thoracic cavity increases, creating a negative pressure there, which draws air into the lungs.

The rectus abdominis, (Latin: straight abdominal) also known as the "abdominal muscle" or simply better known as the "abs", and sometimes informally referred to as the "six-pack", is a pair of segmented skeletal muscle on the ventral aspect of a person's abdomen.
The human brain is the central organ of the nervous system, and with the spinal cord, comprises the central nervous system.
The brain is protected by the skull, suspended in cerebrospinal fluid, and isolated from the bloodstream by the blood–brain barrier.
The heart is a muscular organ found in humans and other animals.
In humans, the heart is approximately the size of a closed fist and is located between the lungs, in the middle compartment of the chest, called the mediastinum.
Other vital organs inside the abdomen include the liver, the kidneys, the pancreas and the spleen.
In humans, the abdomen stretches from the thorax at the thoracic diaphragm to the pelvis at the pelvic brim.
